onscreen_lines.desc: Software & Licensing Includes all digital components required to operate the simulator. 1. Simulation platform: The vendor shall provide comprehensive simulation software that allows users to practice emergency communication scenarios in a realistic, interactive environment. 2. Dispatch and communication interface: The system must include tools that allow users to receive, manage, and respond to simulated emergency requests in a structured and organized manner. 3. Scenario software: The solution shall include a variety of pre-designed simulation scenarios representing different types of emergency situations and levels of complexity. 4. User licenses (student/instructor): The vendor must provide sufficient user access for students and instructors to effectively utilize the system during instruction. 5. Data tracking and reporting tools: The software shall include features that allow instructors to monitor performance, track progress, and evaluate student outcomes.
onscreen_lines.note: Note: This is the maximum rate that Houston ISD will pay for your services. Quotes may be requested when services are needed. Failure to submit a price structure or response to at least one of the proposed price structures under the "Line Items" tab shall constitute a non-responsive bid. Alternatively, the vendor may attach a price list to the "Response Attachments" tab, if needed.

onscreen_lines.desc: Instructional Resources & Curriculum Covers teaching and learning materials aligned to program standards. 1. Lesson plans and pacing guides: The vendor shall provide structured instructional plans that guide educators in delivering the content effectively over time. 2. Scenario library (beginner to advanced): Instructional materials must include a range of scenarios that gradually increase in difficulty to support skill development. 3. Instructor manuals: The vendor shall provide guidance materials to help instructors facilitate lessons, manage simulations, and assess student learning. 4. Student materials (digital/print): The solution must include learner-facing materials that support instruction and reinforce key concepts and skills. 5. Assessment tools and rubrics: The vendor shall include evaluation tools that allow instructors to measure student performance in a consistent and meaningful way.

Alternatively, the vendor may attach a price list to the "Response Attachments" tab, if needed.

onscreen_lines.desc: Equipment & Hardware All physical components are required to run the simulator environment. 1. User workstations: The vendor shall provide or specify equipment that enables participants to engage in the simulation in a realistic workspace setting. 2. Audio communication equipment: The solution must include necessary audio tools to support clear and effective communication during simulations. 3. Instructor control system: The vendor shall provide a means for instructors to manage, monitor, and guide simulation activities in real time. 4. Infrastructure components: The vendor must identify any required infrastructure needed to support system functionality and performance. 5. Installation-related hardware: All components necessary for full setup and operation of the system must be included or clearly specified.

onscreen_lines.desc: Professional Development & Training Services that support educator readiness and implementation. 1. Initial training sessions: The vendor shall provide training to ensure educators are prepared to use and implement the system effectively. 2. Train-the-trainer programs: The vendor should offer training that enables designated staff to support and train additional users internally. 3. Customization training: The vendor shall provide instruction on how to adapt and modify simulation experiences to meet instructional needs. 4. Ongoing professional development: Continued learning opportunities must be available to support long-term program success and effective use of the system.

onscreen_lines.desc: Implementation, Support & Maintenance Combined category covering deployment and ongoing system sustainability. 1. System setup and configuration: The vendor shall ensure the system is properly set up and ready for use upon deployment. 2. Installation of equipment: All physical components must be installed and made fully operational as part of the implementation process. 3. Integration with existing systems: The vendor must ensure compatibility with the organization’s current technology environment. 4. System testing and validation: The vendor shall verify that all components are functioning as intended prior to full use. 5. Help desk and technical support: Ongoing support must be available to assist users with technical issues and system questions. 6. Software updates and upgrades: The vendor shall provide updates to maintain functionality, security, and performance over time. 7. Troubleshooting services: The vendor must address and resolve issues in a timely and effective manner. 8. Equipment warranty coverage: Hardware components shall be supported by warranty protections for a defined period. 9. Service-level agreements (SLAs): The vendor shall define expectations for service responsiveness and system reliability.
